digest.component_or_area: prompt-cache effectiveness warning in structured LLM run
propositions: warn_if_cache_ineffective fires on every small call because its zero/zero predicate has no lower bound and ignores the 4096-token cacheable floor.
Below CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS the zero/zero cache result is expected and non-actionable, so the warning is a false alarm.
The warning contradicts a run's own aggregate telemetry, which can show cache_write_tokens > 0 while per-call lines claim caching had no effect.
Firing ~20 times per review-plan gate run causes alarm fatigue that masks the genuine opus-4-5 silent-cost-bleed defect the warning exists to catch.
The floor constant should have one shared definition consumed by both pass1.py and structured_run.py instead of a duplicated literal.
The zero-cache symptom is specific to the direct-Anthropic path; the same traffic caches correctly on Bedrock.
